no-lead-metrics.label: No visibility on lead response time

pipeline-spreadsheet.label: Job pipeline on a spreadsheet or whiteboard

key-person-risk.label: Pipeline lives in one person's head

no-pipeline-visibility.label: No clear count of stalled jobs

reactive-comms.label: Customers have to call for updates

rep-as-support.label: Sales reps stuck doing customer support

material-coordination.label: Equipment not on site when crew arrives

design-only-tools.label: Design tool, but no ops system

generic-fsm.label: Generic field-service tool, not built for solar

opener.question: Permission-based intro
say: Hey, this is {{me}}. I'll be quick, and this is a cold call, so feel free to hang up on me in 30 seconds.
Mind if I take 30 seconds to tell you why I called, and you tell me if it's worth talking?
opener.why: Saying it's a cold call and asking permission lowers their guard. They get to say yes.

answers.label: Who is this? What's it about?

opener_pitch.question: The 30-second why
say: I work with {{trade}} around Denver on the back-office side, mostly everything that happens after a contract is signed.
Most shops I talk to are great at selling and installing, but jobs get stuck somewhere between signed and PTO, and the status lives in a spreadsheet or in someone's head.
I'm not here to pitch software. I'm trying to figure out if that's true for {{business|your shop}}. Mind if I ask a few quick questions?
opener_pitch.why: Naming a common problem lets them recognize themselves. "Yeah, that's us" is your opening.

opener_gatekeeper.question: Find the right person
say: No worries. I'm trying to reach whoever handles how leads and scheduling work there. Is that the owner or someone else?
When's the best time to catch them?
opener_gatekeeper.why: Get a name and a time. Write both in Notes.

answers.label: Got a name and a time, log a callback

opener_voicemail.question: Voicemail (under 20 seconds)
say: Hi {{contact|there}}, {{me}} here. I help {{trade}} in Denver stop losing jobs that stall between signed and PTO.
I had one specific idea for {{business|your company}}. I'm at [your number]. Again, [your number]. Thanks.
opener_voicemail.why: Follow up in 2 business days. Try 3 times max before moving on.

answers.label: Left it, log a follow-up in 2 days

lead_source.question: Where do most of your leads come from?
lead_source.say: Where do most of your new customers come from right now: referrals, door-knocking, ads, lead vendors?
lead_source.why: Paid and vendor leads are also sold to competitors, so how fast they respond decides who wins the job.

answers.label: We sub for other companies (no own sales)

lead_tracking.question: How are leads tracked?
lead_tracking.say: When a new lead comes in, where does it go? How do you keep track of it?
lead_tracking.why: If leads live in reps' phones, you lose them when the rep leaves, and you can't see what's falling through.

lead_speed.question: How fast does a new lead get a call back?
lead_speed.say: And when a new lead comes in, how fast does someone usually get back to them?
lead_speed.why: Leads called back within minutes convert far better than next-day callbacks. This is often the cheapest fix there is.

sales_proposal.question: How do proposals get built?
sales_proposal.say: Once you've got someone interested, how does the proposal get put together, and how long does that usually take?
sales_proposal.why: Slow proposals let a homeowner's interest cool, and the next installer quotes them first.

answers.label: A few days, back-and-forth with design
Reps build them by hand / templates

sales_followup.question: What happens to unsigned proposals?
sales_followup.say: Quick question: when you send a proposal and don't hear back, what happens next?
sales_followup.why: Stop talking after you ask. "Nothing" or "I try to remember" is the pain.

answers.label: Rep follows up when they remember

sales_close_rate.question: Rough close rate?
sales_close_rate.say: Roughly what share of the proposals you send end up signing?
sales_close_rate.why: If they don't know this number, nobody is watching the funnel.

pipeline_tracking.question: How do you track a job from signed to PTO?
pipeline_tracking.say: Once a contract's signed, there's site survey, design, permitting, interconnection, install, inspection, PTO. How do you keep track of where every job is?
pipeline_tracking.why: This is the core of the audit. Work moves but status doesn't, and that's where the money leaks.

answers.label: Our PM keeps it in their head

pipeline_stuck.question: Where do jobs get stuck the longest?
pipeline_stuck.say: Out of all those stages, where do jobs tend to sit the longest?
pipeline_stuck.why: Each stalled week delays the final payment. Find out which stage stalls and you know where to start.

pipeline_count.question: How many jobs are stalled right now?
pipeline_count.say: If I asked you right now how many jobs are in the pipeline, and how many are stalled, could you tell me?
pipeline_count.why: Not knowing this number off the top of their head is the 'owner dashboard' problem.

comms_updates.question: How do customers get status updates?
comms_updates.say: While all that's happening, how does the homeowner find out where their install is at?
comms_updates.why: Homeowners who hear nothing for weeks start calling, leave bad reviews, or cancel.

comms_calls.question: How many "where's my install?" calls a week?
comms_calls.say: Roughly how many "where's my install?" calls or texts do you get in a week?
comms_calls.why: Each one is 5–10 minutes of someone's time spent looking up status by hand.

crew_scheduling.question: How do surveys and installs get scheduled?
crew_scheduling.say: How do site surveys and installs get on the calendar? Who does the scheduling?
crew_scheduling.why: If the owner is the only one who can schedule, the owner is the bottleneck for every job.

crew_problems.question: Double-bookings or wasted trips?
crew_problems.say: In the last month, any double-bookings or wasted trips? A crew shows up and the permit, the equipment, or the customer isn't ready?
crew_problems.why: A wasted truck roll costs a crew-day. Owners remember these, so ask for a specific story.

money_financing.question: How are financing, deposits, and milestones tracked?
money_financing.say: On the money side: how do you keep track of financing approvals, deposits, and milestone payments?
money_financing.why: Financier milestones (M1, M2, PTO) that nobody tracks mean cash shows up weeks late.

money_commissions.question: How are rep commissions handled?
money_commissions.say: And sales rep commissions: how do those get calculated and paid out?
money_commissions.why: Commission disputes take up the owner's time and drive good reps away.

tools_current.question: What software runs the business today?
tools_current.say: What are you using to run all this today, software-wise?
tools_current.why: Write the exact tool names in Notes. You'll need them for the audit and the build.

tools_fit.question: Do the tools talk to each other?
tools_fit.say: Do those tools talk to each other, or is someone re-typing the same info from one into another?
tools_fit.why: Re-typing data between tools is a quick fix that's easy to show results on.

answers.label: Paying for stuff we don't use

owner_week.question: What eats most of your week?
owner_week.say: Last one, the big one: what eats most of your week?
owner_week.why: This is the pain they feel personally. Write down their exact words, because you'll repeat them in the close.

answers.label: Chasing job status / putting out fires

owner_one_thing.question: If one thing ran itself, what would you pick?
owner_one_thing.say: If one thing in the business just ran itself, what would you pick?
owner_one_thing.why: Their answer is what you sell the audit on. It shows up at the top of the pain summary.
